mainTopic: Whether an עובר's possible share stops a dead כהן's slaves from eating תרומה, and a new משנה on connections that disqualify a woman from תרומה but cannot make her eligible.
overview: A כהן died and left a pregnant widow. The question is whether his slaves may still eat תרומה, since if the עובר is a boy he owns a share of them. The גמרא gives two ways to explain רבי שמעון, who lets the slaves eat. Either he ignores the minority chance that the עובר is a living boy, or בית דין uses רב נחמן's rule to give the עובר a share without slaves. Next comes רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, who says a daughter lets the slaves eat but a son does not. אביי first explains this as a small estate, נכסים מועטים, but רבי יוחנן's ruling knocks that down. So the גמרא rereads 'daughter' as the mother herself, and says the whole ברייתא is רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's. A new משנה then lists five connections, among them the עובר, the יבם and אירוסין, that take a בת כהן away from תרומה but cannot let a בת ישראל eat it. The גמרא starts explaining each item from a פסוק, and the explanation of אירוסין continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First explanation: we do not worry about the minority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its first explanation of רבי שמעון's lenient view. He holds אין חוששין למיעוטא, so we do not worry that the עובר is a living boy who owns a share of the slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: [He holds that] we are not concerned about the minority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence from just before this point. It explains that רבי שמעון lets the slaves eat תרומה because he does not worry about a minority possibility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most pregnancies do not end with a living baby boy who inherits. Roughly half are girls, and some are not born alive. So the chance that the עובר owns part of the slaves is a minority, and רבי שמעון ignores it.

keyTerms.meaning: We are not concerned about the minority (a less likely possibility)
Fetus, an unborn baby
The holy portion of produce that only a כהן and his household may eat

steps.confusionAlert: The 'minority' here is not a minority of people. It is the less likely possibility that the עובר will be a living boy who inherits.

phrases.english: We are not concerned about the minority.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from just before here, explaining why רבי שמעון lets the slaves eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין לְמִיעוּטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an explanation that began just before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the underlying principle (ignoring a minority possibility)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The slaves should not eat, because the עובר might own part of them.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון ignores the minority chance that the עובר is a living male heir.

steps.title: Second explanation: an arrangement keeps the slaves out of the fetus's share
steps.stepSummary: A different answer: רבי שמעון does worry about the minority, but בית דין makes an arrangement (תקנתא), following רב נחמן in the name of שמואל, so that the עובר's share does not include the slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: really he holds that we are concerned about the minority, but we make an arrangement for it, following what רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different explanation of רבי שמעון. It also sets up the next step, where it quotes the rule of רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this answer רבי שמעון agrees the עובר might be a male heir. The fix is practical: the estate is divided now, and the עובר gets a share that has no slaves in it. So the slaves belong only to heirs who can let them eat.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another possible answer
Really, actually: keeps one point while changing the explanation
An arrangement or fix made by the court

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
actually he holds that we are concerned about the minority,
but we make an arrangement for it,
phrases.notes: The arrangement is for the slaves, so they stay out of the עובר's share.

phrases.english: in accordance with what רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר חוֹשְׁשִׁין לְמִיעוּטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the first explanation with a different one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical arrangement instead of ignoring the doubt
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only ignoring the minority could explain רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even if we worry about the minority, בית דין gives the עובר a share without slaves.

steps.title: רב נחמן in the name of שמואל: a guardian divides the estate for orphans
steps.stepSummary: When young orphans want to divide their father's property, בית דין appoints an אפוטרופוס who picks a good share for each one. When they grow up, they may protest the division.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: orphans who came to divide their father's property — the court appoints a guardian for them, and he chooses a fine share for them. When they grow up, they can protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source for the arrangement mentioned in step 2. A guardian can divide an estate for young orphans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the basis for dividing an estate on behalf of someone who cannot act for himself. The same idea is applied to the עובר. In שמואל's version, though, the division is not final: the orphans may object once they grow up.

keyTerms.meaning: Orphans (here, young ones)
A guardian appointed to manage someone's property
To protest or object
They grew up

phrases.english: As רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל:
Orphans who came to divide their father's property —
the court appoints a guardian for them,
and he chooses a fine share for them.
Once they grow up, they can protest.
phrases.notes: They can object to how things were split and have it redone.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the source cited in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית דין may appoint an אפוטרופוס to divide an estate for young orphans, but they may object when grown.

steps.title: רב נחמן's own view: the division is final
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן himself says that once the orphans grow up they cannot protest. Otherwise the court's power would mean nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן himself said: when they grow up, they cannot protest, because if so, what is the strength of the court?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds רב נחמן's own opinion, which goes further than what he reported from שמואל. A division made by בית דין is permanent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב נחמן, a division done by בית דין cannot be undone, because the court's acts must carry weight. This makes the arrangement for the עובר stronger. The slave-free share given to the עובר stays fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: His own (opinion)
The power or authority of the court

phrases.english: And רב נחמן himself said:
once they grow up, they cannot protest,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִם כֵּן מָה כֹּחַ בֵּית דִּין יָפֶה.
phrases.english: for if so, what good is the power of the court?
phrases.notes: "If so" means: if the orphans could undo what the court did.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן דִּידֵיהּ אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with the שמואל version in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A division made by a court-appointed guardian cannot be undone when the orphans grow up.
steps.whyThisMatters: The next step asks whether this rule of רב נחמן, which was used to explain רבי שמעון, is itself argued over by תנאים.

steps.title: Is רב נחמן's rule a dispute between תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי שמעון's view was explained using רב נחמן, the גמרא suggests that the חכמים, who disagree with רבי שמעון, must reject רב נחמן's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב נחמן's rule is a dispute between תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests whether the second explanation forces רב נחמן's rule into one side of an argument between תנאים. The next step answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון lets the slaves eat only because of רב נחמן's arrangement, then the חכמים who forbid it might reject that arrangement. That would make רב נחמן's rule debated by תנאים, not accepted by all.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say: introduces a suggestion that is usually rejected
It is a dispute between תנאים

phrases.english: Shall we say that רב נחמן's rule is a dispute between תנאים?
phrases.notes: The תנאים here are רבי שמעון and the חכמים who argue with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא דְּרַב נַחְמָן תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a possible consequence from the second explanation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the חכמים who argue with רבי שמעון reject רב נחמן's rule?

steps.title: No: everyone accepts רב נחמן, and the argument is about the minority
steps.stepSummary: Everyone accepts רב נחמן's rule. The תנאים only argue about whether to worry about the minority in a case where no arrangement was made.
steps.simpleTranslation: No — everyone agrees with רב נחמן's rule, and here they argue about whether we are concerned about the minority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. רב נחמן's rule is not in dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides are moved back to the first explanation's issue: worrying about the minority. When there is no arrangement, רבי שמעון ignores the minority and the חכמים worry about it. Both would accept a court division like רב נחמן's.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone (all sides of the dispute)
They disagree

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain רבי שמעון: (1) he ignores the minority chance that the עובר is a male heir, or (2) he worries about it, but רב נחמן's court arrangement keeps the slaves out of the עובר's share. Everyone accepts רב נחמן's rule.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן.
phrases.english: No — everyone accepts רב נחמן's rule.
And here they disagree about whether we are concerned about the minority.
phrases.notes: They are arguing about a case where no court division was made.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the תנאים argue about רב נחמן's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute can be explained by a different issue, worrying about the minority, so רב נחמן need not be under debate.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי: a daughter lets the slaves eat, a son does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to another part of the ברייתא. רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, quoting his father, says that if the כהן left a daughter the slaves may eat תרומה, but if he left a son they may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל the son of רבי יוסי says in his father's name: a daughter lets them eat; a son does not let them eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a new opinion from the ברייתא in order to question it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a son, the עובר (if a boy) would share the estate with him, so part of the slaves would belong to the עובר. The ruling about a daughter seems puzzling, and the גמרא will now question it.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of his father
Enables (the slaves) to eat תרומה

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אָבִיו:
phrases.english: רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי says in the name of his father:
a daughter enables them to eat; a son does not enable them to eat.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the dead כהן's slaves, and the food is תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a different opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A surviving daughter lets the slaves eat תרומה; a surviving son does not.

steps.title: Why should the fetus's share block a son but not a daughter?
steps.stepSummary: If a son does not let the slaves eat because of the עובר's share, a daughter should not let them eat either, for the same reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a son, that he does not let them eat? Because of the fetus's share? Then a daughter also should not let them eat, because of the fetus's share!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's distinction. The worry about the עובר seems to apply equally in both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason a son cannot let the slaves eat is that the עובר may own part of them. That same worry exists when there is a daughter. In fact, if the עובר is a boy, he would take the whole estate ahead of a daughter, so the distinction looks backwards.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Asks for the reason behind a distinction
The fetus's share of the inheritance
Also

phrases.english: What is different about a son, that he does not enable them to eat?
Because of the fetus's share?
Then a daughter also should not enable them to eat,
because of the fetus's share!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא בֵּן דְּלֹא מַאֲכִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction stated in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's distinction between a son and a daughter
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason given for the son, the עובר's possible share, applies just as much when there is a daughter.

steps.title: אביי: a small estate, with both a son and a daughter
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ברייתא speaks of נכסים מועטים, where a son and a daughter both exist. Either way, the עובר takes no share, so the slaves eat through the daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We are dealing with a small estate, in a family that has a son and also a daughter. Whichever way it turns out: if the baby she is carrying is a boy, he is no better than the son already here, and that son gets nothing from a small estate. If it is a girl, why does a daughter get anything at all? Only because of a rabbinic enactment. And the רבנן did not make that enactment for a baby that has not yet been born.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from step 8: why should a daughter be different from a son? He sets up a specific case where the unborn baby can never take a share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With נכסים מועטים, the רבנן gave the small estate to the daughters to support them, and the sons get nothing. So if the עובר is a boy, he gets nothing, just like his living brother. If it is a girl, she also gets nothing yet, because the enactment only covers daughters who are already born. Either way the existing daughter alone owns the slaves, and she is a כהן's daughter, so they may eat תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: A small estate, only enough to support the daughters, which the רבנן give to them instead of to the sons
Whichever way you look at it; both possibilities lead to the same result
A rabbinic enactment
The air of the world; being born
A fetus, an unborn baby

steps.confusionAlert: In a small estate it is the daughters who inherit, not the sons. That is the reverse of the normal rule, where sons come first.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Here we are dealing with a small estate.
phrases.notes: A small estate is only enough to support the daughters, so the רבנן gave it to them.

phrases.english: And where there is a son together with a daughter.
Whichever way you look at it:
if this one she is pregnant with is a son,
he is no better than this son who already exists.
If it is a daughter,
why does she get to 'eat' from the estate at all?
phrases.notes: 'Eat' here means getting her support from the estate.

phrases.english: Only through a rabbinic enactment.
As long as it has not come out into the air of the world,
the רבנן did not make the enactment for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָכָא בִּנְכָסִים מוּעָטִים עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 by narrowing the case of the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: אוקימתא: limiting the ברייתא to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A daughter, like a son, should be blocked by the עובר's possible share
steps.terutzMaskana: With a small estate and an existing son, the עובר never takes a share, so the daughter alone owns the slaves

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא does not fit a small estate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי from the ברייתא's last line, which says daughters get nothing when there is a son. With a small estate, the daughters get everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain the ברייתא? As a small estate. But look at the end of it: 'Perhaps the fetus will turn out to be a boy, and daughters get nothing where there is a son.' The opposite is true! A small estate belongs to the daughters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's explanation using a line from the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ending says a son pushes the daughters out. That is the normal inheritance rule. But in אביי's case of נכסים מועטים, the daughters push the sons out. So the ending cannot be talking about a small estate, and that seems to undercut אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you set up (explain) the source?
The end clause of a source
On the contrary

phrases.english: How did you set up the ברייתא?
As dealing with a small estate.
Say the end clause:
'Perhaps the fetus will be found to be male,
and daughters have nothing where there is a son.'
On the contrary!
A small estate belongs to the daughters!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אוֹקֵימְתַּאּ בִּנְכָסִים מוּעָטִים, אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's case setup from step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the ברייתא is about נכסים מועטים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא assumes sons push daughters out, but in a small estate daughters push sons out, so the ברייתא cannot be about a small estate

steps.title: The end clause is about a large estate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the end of the ברייתא switches to a different case: a large estate.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end clause, we have moved on to a large estate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי by saying the ברייתא's last line is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With נכסים מרובין, a large estate, the normal rule applies and the sons inherit, so daughters get nothing where there is a son. The first part of the ברייתא can still be about a small estate, so אביי's explanation stands.

keyTerms.meaning: We have come to; the source now moves to a different case
A large estate, where the sons inherit by the normal rule

phrases.english: In the end clause we have come to a large estate.

steps.triggerLanguage: סֵיפָא אֲתָאן לִנְכָסִים מְרוּבִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the ברייתא: the first part and the end clause speak of different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole ברייתא must be about the same kind of estate
steps.terutzMaskana: The first part is a small estate and the end clause is a large estate

steps.title: Does a small estate really belong to the daughters?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that a small estate belongs to the daughters. רבי יוחנן rules that if the sons sell it, the sale stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a small estate really belong to the daughters? But רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if the orphan sons went ahead and sold a small estate, what they sold is sold!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge against the basic idea underneath אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sons' sale of a small estate is valid, then the sons still own it. The daughters only have a right to be supported from it. In that case the slaves belong to the sons too, and the problem of a son blocking the slaves from eating תרומה comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Orphans; here, the dead man's sons
Who went ahead and sold
What they sold is sold; the sale is valid

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge goes after the root of אביי's answer: does the enactment for daughters give them real ownership, or only a right to support?

phrases.english: And does a small estate belong to the daughters?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But didn't רבי אסי say in the name of רבי יוחנן:
Orphans who went ahead and sold
from a small estate,
what they sold is sold?!
phrases.notes: So the sons still own the property; the daughters were only promised support from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּנְכָסִים מוּעָטִים דְּבָנוֹת נִינְהוּ? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind steps 9 through 11 that a small estate belongs to the daughters
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that נכסים מועטים belong to the daughters
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן rules that the sons' sale of a small estate is valid, which shows the sons still own it, so a son should still block the slaves

steps.title: The 'daughter' in the ברייתא is really the mother
steps.stepSummary: Since the small-estate reading failed, the גמרא now explains that 'daughter' means the pregnant widow herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does the 'daughter' mentioned in the ברייתא mean? It means the mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on אביי's explanation, which ran into רבי יוחנן's ruling. It offers a new reading: the word 'daughter' points to the mother, the widow herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'daughter' here is the woman, not a child of the dead כהן. She can let her own נכסי מלוג slaves eat, because the עובר has no share in her property. The son cannot let the נכסי צאן ברזל slaves eat, because the עובר owns a share in those.

keyTerms.meaning: Mother; here, the pregnant widow herself
'Rather': drops the earlier explanation and offers a new one
The wife's own property; the husband only uses its profits, and his heirs have no share in it
Property the wife brought in that the husband took over and guaranteed; his heirs, including the עובר, share in it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not picture a little girl here. The 'daughter' is the woman, the pregnant widow herself, called בת simply because she is a female.

phrases.english: Rather, what is the 'daughter' that it teaches?
phrases.notes: This is the word 'daughter' from רבי ישמעאל's line: 'a daughter lets them eat, a son does not.'

phrases.english: A mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא, מַאי ״בַּת״ דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops אביי's small-estate answer, which step 12 knocked down, and rereads the word 'daughter'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a word in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Daughter' meant the dead man's daughter, inheriting a small estate.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Daughter' means the mother, who lets her own מלוג slaves eat because the עובר has no share in them.

steps.title: Then this is the same as רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: If 'daughter' means the mother, רבי ישמעאל's line just repeats what רבי יוסי already said in the first part.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this is just רבי יוסי's view!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the new reading. If the mother lets her מלוג slaves eat, that is exactly what רבי יוסי already taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא usually does not quote a second תנא just to repeat the first one. If רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי adds nothing new, why is he quoted at all?

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so': if we accept that reading, a problem follows
'That is the same as': nothing new is being added

phrases.english: If so,
this is the same as רבי יוסי!
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי already said in the first part of the ברייתא that the widow's מלוג slaves may eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַיְינוּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading just given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'daughter' means the mother
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading makes רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's statement a plain repeat of רבי יוסי's.

steps.title: The whole ברייתא belongs to רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: There is no repeat. The entire ברייתא is taught by רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole ברייתא is taught by רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי is not adding a second opinion. He is the one who teaches the whole ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since it is all one teaching, nothing is repeated. The son's slaves do not eat because of the עובר's share. The mother's own slaves do eat. This wraps up the discussion of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'All of it': the entire ברייתא
'Teaches it': he is the one who teaches it

steps.whatToRemember: Final reading: the widow lets her own מלוג slaves eat תרומה. The heirs cannot let the צאן ברזל slaves eat, because the עובר has a share in them. The whole ברייתא is רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's.

phrases.english: The whole of it, רבי ישמעאל
the son of רבי יוסי teaches it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלָּהּ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'repeat' challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Who said it: one תנא teaches the whole ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two separate תנאים were quoted, so the second one must add something.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is one teaching from one תנא, so nothing is repeated.

steps.title: משנה: five who disqualify but cannot make her eligible
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists five connections that take a כהן's daughter out of תרומה but cannot bring a בת ישראל into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The fetus, the יבם, betrothal, the deaf-mute, and a boy of nine years and one day disqualify her, but they do not let her eat.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists five cases where a man's link to a woman is strong enough to take away her right to eat תרומה, but too weak to give her that right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Take a כהן's daughter tied to a ישראל through one of these: she loses תרומה. Now take a בת ישראל tied to a כהן the same way: she does not gain תרומה. Taking away is easier than giving.

keyTerms.meaning: A fetus, still in its mother's womb
The brother of a man who died without children
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
A deaf-mute, whose marriage is only a rabbinic one
They disqualify her from eating תרומה
They make her eligible to eat תרומה

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key rule: a weak connection can take away the right to eat תרומה but cannot give it.

phrases.english: משנה:
The fetus, and the יבם, and betrothal,
phrases.notes: The fetus is one left behind when the husband died or divorced her while she was pregnant.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַחֵרֵשׁ, וּבֶן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד —
phrases.english: and the deaf-mute, and a boy of nine years and one day,
disqualify, but do not let her eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָעוּבָּר, וְהַיָּבָם, וְהָאֵירוּסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the ברייתא discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These five connections disqualify a כהן's daughter from תרומה but do not let a בת ישראל eat it.

steps.title: Doubtful age and doubtful maturity
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds cases of doubt: maybe the boy is nine years and a day, and maybe he has grown two hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is unclear whether he is nine years and one day old or not. It is unclear whether he has grown two hairs or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes on to doubtful cases. We are not sure if the boy reached nine years and a day, or if he grew the two hairs that make him an adult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two-hairs doubt matters for a boy who betrothed a woman, since only an adult's betrothal counts. In both doubts the same rule as before applies: he disqualifies her but does not let her eat.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt; we do not know which way it is
Two pubic hairs, the sign that a boy has become an adult

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק שֶׁהוּא בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: It is unclear whether he is nine years and one day old
or whether he is not;
it is unclear whether he has grown two hairs
phrases.notes: The משנה does not say the ruling again here. It carries over: these also disqualify but do not let her eat.

phrases.english: or whether he has not grown them.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָפֵק שֶׁהוּא בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד סָפֵק שֶׁאֵינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the משנה's rule to doubtful cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the boy's age or adulthood is in doubt, he still disqualifies her and still cannot let her eat.

steps.title: House collapse: who died first?
steps.stepSummary: A man and his wife, his brother's daughter, die when a house falls on them. Nobody knows who died first, so the other wife does חליצה, not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a house fell on a man and on his brother's daughter, and it is not known which one died first, her צרה does חליצה and does not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a case of doubt about the order of death. The rival wife must do חליצה and may not do יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dead man's brother is the father of the wife who died. If she outlived her husband, even for a moment, the other wife is a צרת ערוה and is fully exempt. If she died first, the other wife needs יבום or חליצה. Because of the doubt, she does חליצה just in case and cannot do יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: A co-wife; another wife of the same man
She performs חליצה, which releases her from the יבם
She enters into יבום, marrying the brother
His brother's daughter, his niece

steps.confusionAlert: Do not forget who the יבם is here: he is the father of the wife who died. That is why her death order decides everything for the other wife.

phrases.aramaic: נָפַל הַבַּיִת עָלָיו וְעַל בַּת אָחִיו,
phrases.english: If the house fell on him and on his brother's daughter,
phrases.notes: His brother's daughter is his wife, and her father is the brother who would do יבום.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין יָדוּעַ אֵי זֶה מֵת רִאשׁוֹן —
phrases.english: and it is not known which one died first,
her rival wife does חליצה and does not do יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפַל הַבַּיִת עָלָיו וְעַל בַּת אָחִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case of doubt to the משנה, this time about who died first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When it is unclear whether the niece-wife died before her husband, the rival wife does חליצה and not יבום.

steps.title: An unborn baby disqualifies a כהן's daughter from תרומה
steps.stepSummary: A בת כהן married to a ישראל whose husband died while she is pregnant cannot go back to eating תרומה. The פסוק says 'כנעוריה', like in her youth, and that excludes a pregnant woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The unborn baby. If she is a כהן's daughter married to a ישראל, the baby disqualifies her. The פסוק says 'as in her youth', which leaves out a pregnant woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the first item in the משנה's list, the unborn baby. It shows why the baby keeps a כהן's daughter from returning to תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a בת כהן whose ישראל husband dies with no children goes back to eating תרומה in her father's house. The Torah adds the word 'כנעוריה', like when she was young. A pregnant woman is not like she was in her youth, so she does not go back.

keyTerms.meaning: An unborn baby
Disqualifies her from eating תרומה
'As in her youth', a word from the פסוק about a כהן's daughter returning home
A pregnant woman

phrases.english: GEMARA: The unborn baby.

phrases.aramaic: אִי בַּת כֹּהֵן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא — פָּסֵיל לָהּ.
phrases.english: If she is a כהן's daughter married to a ישראל, it disqualifies her.
phrases.notes: Her husband died while she was pregnant, so the question is whether she can go back to eating תרומה.

phrases.english: 'As in her youth' leaves out a pregnant woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: גמרא העובר אי בת כהן לישראל היא פסיל לה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the new משנה from step 16 and explains its first item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pregnant בת כהן widowed from a ישראל does not go back to תרומה, based on 'כנעוריה'.

steps.title: An unborn baby cannot let a בת ישראל eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: If a בת ישראל married to a כהן is widowed while pregnant, the unborn baby does not let her eat תרומה. Only a child who is already born can do that.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she is a ישראל's daughter married to a כהן, the baby does not let her eat. A born child lets her eat; one not yet born does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half of the rule for the unborn baby: it cannot bring a בת ישראל into תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A living child of a כהן can keep his mother, a בת ישראל, eating תרומה after his father dies. But that power only belongs to a child who is already born. A baby still in the womb does not count yet.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-כהן woman married to a כהן
Lets someone eat תרומה
A child who has already been born

phrases.aramaic: אִי בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכֹהֵן הִיא — לֹא מַאֲכִיל לָהּ,
phrases.english: If she is a ישראל's daughter married to a כהן, it does not let her eat;
a child who was born lets her eat,
one who was not born does not let her eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אי בת ישראל לכהן היא לא מאכיל לה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the unborn baby by giving the other side of the rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a born child can let his mother, a בת ישראל, eat תרומה; an unborn baby cannot.

steps.title: A יבם who is a ישראל disqualifies a כהן's daughter
steps.stepSummary: A בת כהן whose ישראל husband died childless, and who is waiting for a ישראל יבם, cannot go back to eating תרומה. The פסוק 'ושבה אל בית אביה' leaves out a שומרת יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The יבם. If she is a כהן's daughter tied to a ישראל, he disqualifies her. 'And she returns to her father's house' leaves out a woman waiting for her יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second item in the משנה, the יבם. It explains why a ישראל יבם keeps a כהן's daughter from returning to תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lets a בת כהן eat תרומה again only when she 'returns to her father's house'. A woman waiting for יבום is still tied to her husband's family through the יבם. So she has not really returned to her father's house.

keyTerms.meaning: The brother of a man who died childless, who may marry the widow
'And she returns to her father's house', from the פסוק
A widow waiting for her יבם to do יבום or חליצה

phrases.english: The יבם.

phrases.aramaic: אִי בַּת כֹּהֵן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא — פָּסֵיל לָהּ.
phrases.english: If she is a כהן's daughter tied to a ישראל יבם, he disqualifies her.
'And she returns to her father's house'
leaves out a woman waiting for her יבם.

steps.triggerLanguage: היבם אי בת כהן לישראל היא פסיל לה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same two-sided explanation to the next item on the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומרת יבם has not 'returned to her father's house', so she cannot eat תרומה.

steps.title: A יבם who is a כהן cannot let a בת ישראל eat
steps.stepSummary: A בת ישראל waiting for a יבם who is a כהן cannot eat תרומה because of him. The Torah says 'קנין כספו', his own acquisition, and she was acquired by his brother, not by him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she is a ישראל's daughter tied to a כהן יבם, he does not let her eat. The Torah says 'the purchase of his money', and she is his brother's acquisition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second half of the rule for the יבם: a כהן יבם cannot bring a בת ישראל into תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן can feed תרומה to someone he himself acquired, as the פסוק says 'קנין כספו'. The bond between the widow and the יבם came from his brother's marriage, not from anything the יבם did. So she does not count as his acquisition.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The purchase of his money', the פסוק showing a כהן feeds those he acquired
'The Merciful One', a name for ה׳ as the One who gave the Torah
His brother's acquisition

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean she is not connected to the יבם at all. She is tied to him, which is why she cannot marry someone else, but that bond is not his own קנין, so it does not let her eat תרומה.

phrases.aramaic: אִי בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכֹהֵן הִיא — לָא מַאֲכֵיל לָהּ,
phrases.english: If she is a ישראל's daughter tied to a כהן יבם, he does not let her eat,
the Merciful One said 'the purchase of his money',
and this woman is his brother's acquisition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אי בת ישראל לכהן היא לא מאכיל לה קנין כספו אמר רחמנא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the יבם by giving the other side of the rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן יבם cannot feed a widow who is a בת ישראל תרומה, since she is his brother's קנין, not his own.

steps.title: Betrothal to a ישראל disqualifies a כהן's daughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining the third item, אירוסין. A בת כהן who is betrothed to a ישראל is disqualified from תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And betrothal. If she is a כהן's daughter betrothed to a ישראל, he disqualifies her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the third item in the משנה, אירוסין, and starts with the side that disqualifies. This sets up the next part, which will continue the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like the first two items, the גמרא first states that betrothal to a ישראל takes a כהן's daughter out of תרומה. The reason and the other side of the rule continue in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
A betrothed woman
A כהן's daughter connected to a non-כהן

phrases.english: And the betrothal.

phrases.aramaic: אִי בַּת כֹּהֵן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא — פָּסֵיל לָהּ,
phrases.english: If she is a כהן's daughter betrothed to a ישראל, he disqualifies her,

steps.triggerLanguage: והאירוסין אי בת כהן לישראל היא פסיל לה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same pattern with the third item on the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Betrothal to a ישראל takes a כהן's daughter out of eating תרומה.
